claim_being_audited: Whether the model can be cleanly certified for launch on the current record, based on aggregate readiness, rehearsal results, and general operational checks, despite missing evaluation coverage for the named deployment context of technician safety-note routing.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold for certification.
Passing aggregate readiness and launch rehearsal supports readiness but does not substitute for named-context evaluation coverage.
If a named deployment context lacks evaluation coverage, the gap must be disclosed, resolved, or covered by approved risk acceptance before clean certification.
Public guidance on documentation and risk management is supportive context, not proof that policy predicates were met in this case.
A certification conclusion must rest on admissible evidence of policy compliance, not on plausible rationale alone.
evidence_requests: Final model-card or certification artifact showing explicit disclosure of the technician safety-note routing evaluation gap.
Approved risk-acceptance record covering the missing technician safety-note routing evals before launch.
Completed technician safety-note routing evaluation results for the current launch configuration.
Evidence showing whether technician safety-note routing is material to the named launch use case under the release policy.
specific_concerns: Admissible evidence supports aggregate launch readiness, but not a clean certification without disclosure for all named deployment contexts.
Technician safety-note routing is explicitly named in the deployment plan, and its evals are absent from the packet.
General support, latency, and rollback checks expressly do not cover technician safety-note routing.
Policy requires disclosure of material limitations or evaluation gaps for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The draft model-card statement treating missing evals as effectively non-limiting is contradicted by QA's view that missing evals should be treated as unknown rather than passed.
No admissible evidence shows the gap was resolved, disclosed in final certification materials, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
unsupported_claims: A clean certification is fully supported for all named deployment contexts on the current packet.
Technician safety-note routing can be treated as passed or non-limiting because no completed test has failed.
Public guidance alone is sufficient to justify certification despite an unresolved named-context evaluation gap.
The recommended action certify_model is supported without an accompanying limitation or gap disclosure.
